requirements.note: Inset-grouped History, newest first, with name, date, exercise count and volume (e.g. Legs, Sun Oct 25, 4 exercises · 6,767.5 lb). It also has a native search field and a '61 workouts' footer.
Detail shows a summary (date, exercises, sets, total volume), then a section per exercise with muscle · equipment · volume and its sets as 'reps × weight'.

The Workout tab opens a system alert to name the workout (Start stays disabled while the name is empty). The Add Exercise sheet has a muscle filter as a pull-down menu, a bottom search field, and lists grouped by muscle; filter and search combine. Add Set is a sheet with a number pad, prefilled from the previous set, and checks weight from 0 to 2,000 lb. Tapping a set edits it and offers Delete Set; swipe-to-delete works. More menu has Rename and Discard. Finish stays disabled until a set is logged; finishing pushes the new workout's detail and it appears at the top of History.
Library tab: a large-title inset-grouped list in muscle sections with a chevron on each row. It has no search, which this requirement does not ask for.

Exercise screen shows muscle and equipment, a Best Set card (heaviest weight, reps, which workout and date) and the workouts it appears in, with their sets. It updated straight away with a newly finished heavier set.
After relaunch, the workout in progress kept its name, exercise and edited/deleted sets; the finished workout stayed in History and in the exercise's best set.

tells: The Add Set sheet header is not a real navigation bar: the title is regular weight instead of semibold, and Cancel is a bare blue X while Save is a glass checkmark, so the two buttons don't match.
Workout detail and exercise screens use a small inline title, while the root screens use large titles. This is acceptable, but B keeps the large title on detail.
Finish has no confirmation and jumps straight to the finished workout's detail. That is abrupt, but not wrong.
A.scroll: History (61 rows) and Library (120 rows) scroll like native lists: smooth flings, no blank or popping rows, a normal rubber-band at both ends, and scroll position kept when switching tabs.

requirements.note: Inset-grouped History, newest first, with a '60 workouts' header. Each row shows name, date, an exercise count with a list icon and volume with a scale icon. There is no search on History.
Detail keeps the large title and shows a summary card. Each exercise is a tinted section header that links to the exercise and shows its volume, with sets below as 'N reps × W lb'.

A '+' in History opens the workout as a sheet: an inline name field, a started time and Add Exercises. The picker is multi-select with checkmark circles, a search field, muscle filter chips and an 'Add (n)' button. Add Set uses text fields plus system steppers (5 lb steps). Tapping a set opens Edit Set with Delete Set; swipe-to-delete works; each exercise's ellipsis menu has Remove Exercise. Hide shows a 'Workout in Progress – Resume' card in History. Finish asks for confirmation in a popover, summarises the workout and warns that exercises without sets will be left out; the finished workout then appears in History.
Library tab is grouped by muscle, with a search field and a filter-by-muscle toolbar button.
Exercise screen shows muscle and equipment, a Best Set card (weight, reps, workout and date) and the workouts it appears in with their sets, plus a count footer. It updated with the new workout.
After relaunch, the workout in progress kept its name, sets and the edit and delete, and the app reopened straight into it. The finished workout stayed in History.

bugs: On an exercise screen opened from a workout, that workout's row in the 'Workouts' list stays highlighted grey and never clears (a stuck selection).
tells: The stuck grey selection highlight on the exercise screen's workout row.
In the exercise screen's list of sets, a set breaks across lines ('6 ×' / '27.5 lb') at the default text size.
The muscle filter chips in the picker are hand-made capsules that run off the right edge, followed by a large empty gap before the list.
Library uses a small inline title while History uses a large one, so the two tabs don't match.
Exercise headers on workout detail are tinted links with a separate faded-tint volume, which looks a little web-like.
B.scroll: History and Library scroll smoothly with native deceleration and bounce; no blank rows or jumps, and position is kept across tabs.

why: Both apps meet every requirement, persist correctly, and handle dark mode and the largest text size well. B has some nicer touches (multi-select picker, steppers, a finish confirmation, Resume from History), but it also has a stuck selection highlight, a set that breaks mid-expression, and hand-made chips with odd spacing. A is more consistent and cleaner throughout, so it edges ahead.
